chunks: It is narrated from Saʿīd al-Aʿraj that he said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be your ransom, I may be in the Witr prayer, and I may already have intended the fast, and I may be in supplication, and I fear dawn, and I dislike cutting off my supplication for myself and drinking water, while the water jug is before me.
He said: So he said to me, “Then step toward it one step, two steps, or three, and drink, and return to your place, and do not cut off your supplication for yourself.”

key_terms.الصَّوْمَ: the intended fast to begin at dawn
key_terms.الْخُطْوَةَ: a step taken toward the water vessel
key_terms.الْفَجْرَ: dawn, the beginning time of the fast
key_terms.الْقُلَّةُ: the water jug or vessel placed nearby
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water to be drunk before dawn
key_terms.الْوِتْرِ: the Witr prayer performed in the night prayer

ai.seo_question: Can a person take a few steps and drink water during Witr supplication before dawn without interrupting the du'a?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a practical ruling related to Witr prayer, duʿa, and the pre-dawn time for fasting. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام permits taking a few steps to drink water during the supplication without breaking off the duʿa, showing facilitation in worship while observing the fast.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1421 - It is narrated from Sa'id al-A'raj that He said:
I said to Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)
"May I be your ransom, sometimes I am in the Witr prayer and have already intended to fast. I am engaged in supplication and I fear the approach of dawn, but I dislike interrupting my supplication to drink water, and there is a water jug in front of me."
Imam (as) said to me: "Take a step, two, or three towards it, drink, and then return to your place without interrupting your supplication."
